title: lightningcss ate my precision
impact: Anyone whose CSS has numbers with more than 6 significant digits, which is common in Sass output (10 digits by default), Bootstrap 3 (line-height 1.428571429) and grid percentages (33.333333%). Visible effects are 1px shifts and gaps in layout. 6 reactions on the issue plus 3 thumbs-up on comments, 3 commenters. Same root cause: #917 (closed 2025-04-22, asked for f64) and #1394 (open, newer, more detailed: also covers 1234.5678px and exponent output).
code: cssparser 0.37 serializer: ToCss for f32 / write_numeric -> dtoa_short::write (6 significant digits)
summary: Every number is printed with 6 significant digits, minified or not, so 1.3333333333 becomes 1.33333, 33.333333% becomes 33.3333% and calc(4/3) becomes 1.33333. Chromium computes these values at higher precision than it serializes them: 1.33333 x 12px lays out as 15.984375px rather than 16px, and 33.3333% of 300px as 99.984375px rather than 100px. So the output renders differently, even though CSSOM serialization in Chromium also shows 6 digits. Printing the shortest decimal that round-trips the stored f32 (1.3333334, 33.333332%) gives the same layout as the source in Chromium.
repro: 949-repro.mjs: '.a{line-height:1.3333333333}.b{line-height:calc(4/3)}.c{width:33.333333%}.d{line-height:1.428571429}' with minify -> '.a,.b{line-height:1.33333}.c{width:33.3333%}.d{line-height:1.42857}' on master, 1.14.0 and 1.33.0. Custom properties too: '--x:1.3333333333' -> '--x: 1.33333' (also unminified). Browser check: 949-in.css + 949-fixture.html, output in 949-equivalence.txt.
evidence: repro.mjs: local (master), 1.14.0 and 1.33.0 identical, so this is long-standing behavior, not a regression. probe.mjs (Chrome 153), height of an element with 12px font: line-height 1.33333 -> 15.984375, 1.333333 -> 15.984375, 1.3333333 / 1.3333334 / 1.3333333333 -> 16. Width of a 300px flex child: 33.3333% / 33.33333% -> 99.984375, 33.333332% / 33.333333% / 33.333334% -> 100. Chromium serializes parse('line-height','1.3333333333') as '1.33333' and calc(4/3) as 'calc(1.33333)', which matches the maintainer's earlier comment. equivalence.mjs --minify on the fixture: exit 1, NOT EQUIVALENT (heights 18px -> 18.9844px etc.), but the 99.98 vs 100 width differences are classed as 'rounding' and not counted. Spec: CSSOM 'Serializing CSS values' says '... rounding the value if necessary to not produce more than 6 decimals'. That covers CSSOM serialization of specified values, which browsers evidently do not use for layout. It doesn't license a build tool to change the value it computes from.

fix.approach: Print numbers as the shortest decimal that reads back as the same f32 (e.g. via ryu, or Rust's f32 Display plus CSS formatting rules) in lightningcss's own number and dimension serialization instead of cssparser's 6-digit dtoa_short. This also needs exponent handling (#1394) and updates to many expected outputs in src/lib.rs, and costs a few bytes per long number. An opt-in precision option is the alternative the reporter asked for, but it would be a new API.

draftReply:
Thanks, and thanks everyone for the extra cases. I checked this in Chromium: it serializes `1.3333333333` as `1.33333`, as noted above, but it lays out with more precision. With `font-size: 12px`, `line-height: 1.33333` gives a 15.984375px box where `1.3333333333` gives 16px. Likewise `33.3333%` of 300px is 99.984375px where `33.333333%` is 100px. So rounding to 6 significant digits can visibly change layout, which matches the 1px shifts reported here. Keeping enough digits to preserve the stored value (`1.3333334`) renders the same as the source. Whether to change the default number output is up to the maintainer. In the meantime, writing `calc(4 / 3)` doesn't help, because it gets folded to the same rounded value. #1394 covers the same root cause.
